title: Open-Domain Aspect-Opinion Co-Mining with Double-Layer Span Extraction

problem.claim: Aspect-opinion extraction requires extracting aspect terms and opinion terms, and open-domain settings also require mining their correspondence.

gap.claim: Supervised methods require large-scale human-annotated training data, restricting their use in open-domain tasks because such data is unavailable.

contributions.claim: The work introduces ODAO, a joint open-domain method for mining aspect terms, opinion terms, and their correspondence with a double-layer span extraction framework.
ODAO generates weak labels for unannotated corpora using rules based on universal dependency parsing instead of human annotations.
ODAO uses canonical correlation analysis for early stopping under noisy weak supervision and self-training to address weak-supervision bias.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the power of ODAO.
On four benchmark datasets for aspect-opinion co-extraction and pair extraction, the authors report competitive or better performance than state-of-the-art fully supervised methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Aspect-opinion extraction targets aspect terms and opinion terms, with correspondence also relevant to the addressed task.
Although supervised methods perform strongly, their dependence on large-scale annotations limits open-domain use.
ODAO combines weak-label generation, double-layer span extraction, early stopping, and self-training to extract terms and aspect-opinion pairs.
The authors report extensive experiments and competitive or better benchmark results against fully supervised methods.

source_observation.claim: Weak labels generated from rules based on universal dependency parsing are used to train extraction models on unannotated corpora.

interpretation.claim: Structured linguistic rules can provide a supervision substitute when domain-specific annotations are unavailable.

application.claim: For a new open-domain extraction task, consider generating initial weak labels from broadly applicable dependency-based rules before iterative model training.

exception.claim: Weak supervision introduces noise and bias, requiring explicit mitigation such as early stopping and self-training.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the double-layer span architecture in detail.
